comments.body:
## FIXED — Gerrit 1343. Three of the four ACs are met; the live one waits on a harness run.

`_peer_removed_the_parent()` gates the outbound parent SET in `diff_canonical_fields`: suppress only when the local parent is set, the remote has none, AND the observed peer parent still EQUALS the local one. `get_peer_parent` stays getattr-guarded, so a legacy store falls through to the previous unconditional push.

**Gates:** 2170 reconciler tests pass, ruff clean, mypy 429, hygiene 0, `outbound_field_diff.py` 458/800.

### THE IMPLEMENTER REPORTED A CONTRADICTION AND WAS RIGHT TO — I had predicted the wrong casualty

I warned it that guard 4 (`test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear`) would likely go red and told it not to touch it. **Guard 4 passed untouched.** It hand-builds `_FakeOutbound`, so it never calls the outbound differ and the fix cannot reach it.

What went red instead was the **diagnostic cell in the new module** — the one I said must stay green. And that is logically forced, not a regression: that cell CHARACTERISED link 1 of the defect ("outbound DOES emit parent here"), which is precisely what the fix removes. A defect-characterisation test cannot survive its own defect being fixed; the two are contradictory over the same fixture by construction. The agent identified this correctly, left both cells untouched as instructed, and handed the decision back.

### What I did with it

**Inverted the diagnostic cell into a regression guard**: outbound must emit NO parent write when the peer removed it. That is a SHARPER guard than the primary cell — the primary asserts the outcome (the local parent ends up cleared), this asserts the mechanism (the contradicting write is never produced). Restoring the re-push reddens it immediately, whereas the primary could in principle be rescued by some unrelated change to inbound's filter.

**Added the opposite-direction cell**, which is the one that stops this fix becoming a worse bug. Suppressing on an empty remote parent ALONE would green everything else here and silently discard real local intent — 'the peer wins a removal it made' quietly becoming 'the peer always wins', which is data loss. `test_outbound_STILL_pushes_a_parent_the_local_side_re_set` holds the scenario identical except the OBSERVED PEER PARENT, and requires the push. It passes, so the suppression is discriminating on evidence rather than on a falsy remote.

**Narrowed guard 4's docstring** rather than its assertion. Its scenario is now specifically the local-re-set case — the one where suppression IS correct — and it records that it fabricates its input, which is exactly why it could never have caught this.

- [x] `test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass` GREEN
- [x] a genuinely re-set local parent still wins outbound
- [ ] `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` GREEN on a live run — needs the next harness run
- [x] guard 4 reworded to the local-re-set case

## AC3 IS MET — the live inbound clear round-trips. Run 30874380112.

`test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is **GONE from the failure list**. It failed in both previous runs; with the suppression fix present it passes.

    round 2 (no fix):  5 failed, 52 passed  — inbound clear RED
    round 3 (fix):     4 failed, 56 passed  — inbound clear GREEN

So the mechanism proven in the unit harness — outbound re-pushing a parent the peer had removed, and inbound discarding its own clear as a same-pass contradiction — was the real cause on a live instance too, and suppressing the re-push resolves it end to end. 88d9's parent clear is reachable in a bidirectional pass for the first time.

All four ACs met.

compiled_state.description:
# 88d9's inbound parent-clear is unreachable in a bidirectional pass: outbound re-pushes the parent and inbound discards its own clear

A parent cleared on the Jira side is never cleared locally. The inbound clear that ticket
88d9 built is COMPUTED and then DISCARDED within the same pass, so `.parent_id` survives
indefinitely on a child whose remote parent is gone.

## Proven RED-first, not inferred

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_clear_bidirectional_37e7.py` wires the REAL
outbound differ into the REAL inbound differ the way `run_differs` does — deliberately NOT a
hand-built outbound entry, which is the flaw that hid this. Two cells, first run, no setup
fighting:

    test_real_outbound_differ_emits_a_parent_write_for_the_deparented_child   PASSED
    test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass                     FAILED

      outbound fields for DC-1: {'parent': 'DC-2'}
      inbound fields for DC-1:  {}
      inbound items suppressed by outbound context: 1
      RECON: outbound_update key=DC-1 changed=[parent] comments=0 labels=0 links=0

`suppressed == 1` is the smoking gun: inbound computed exactly one item — the clear — and it
was thrown away.

## Mechanism, both steps read from source

1. **Outbound re-pushes the parent.** `outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent` resolves the
   bound epic parent; `canonical_remote["remote_parent_id"]` is now `None`; they differ, so the
   local-wins branch emits `changed["parent"] = <parent key>`. Crucially `parent` is NOT in
   `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`, so no baseline arbitration ever defers to inbound on this field.
2. **Inbound discards its own clear.** `inbound_differ` canonicalizes the outbound `parent` to
   `parent_id`, then the contradiction filter drops every key already present in the outbound
   entry — including the clear it just computed.

The clear's precondition (Jira has no parent, local does) is IDENTICAL to the outbound
re-push's precondition. So for any parent rebar can resolve outbound — bound, and epic-typed
per bug 8b25's guard — 88d9's clear can never fire in a bidirectional pass.

## Why the existing 88d9 suite is green

Every 88d9 acceptance cell passes `outbound_mutations=None`. The single cell that DOES supply
outbound context — `test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear` — hand-builds a
fake outbound entry and asserts the suppression as DESIRED behaviour. It never asks whether the
real outbound differ produces that mutation in the clear scenario. It always does.

That is this epic's signature failure shape one level up: not a vacuous oracle, but a REAL
oracle asserting the wrong thing because its input was fabricated rather than produced.

## Scope

Confirmed for the EPIC-parent case, which is the normal one on Data Center. For a non-epic
local parent `_resolve_local_parent` omits the parent entirely, outbound emits nothing, and the
suppression cannot fire — that is the separate situation [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] covers.

## Blast radius beyond DC

The suppression lives in the SHARED differ layer, not in a vendor adapter, so Jira Cloud is
implicated on the same code path wherever a parent is cleared remotely while the local parent
still resolves. Not yet observed there — recorded as a question, not a claim.

## Proposed fix (from the trace, not yet implemented)

Give the outbound parent branch the directionality guard the mirrored fields already have,
reusing 88d9's own evidence channel: before emitting a parent SET, suppress when `local_parent`
is truthy, `remote_parent` is falsy, AND `binding_store.get_peer_parent(local_id) ==
local_parent` — i.e. the peer de-parented since our last observation while local stood still,
which is exactly the case `diff_inbound_parent` exists to handle. `get_peer_parent` must stay
getattr-guarded, and its absence must fall through to today's local-wins push.

Guard 4 (`test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear`) then needs restating as
"an outbound push suppresses the clear ONLY when local re-set the parent", rather than
unconditionally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass` is GREEN
- [ ] a local parent that was genuinely re-set still wins outbound — the fix must not invert
      into "remote always wins", which would silently drop real local intent
- [ ] `test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_round_trips` is GREEN on a live harness run,
      with the run id recorded
- [ ] the reworded guard 4 asserts suppression only for the local-re-set case
